messages:
maria: Heads-up — we saw a cluster-wide spike in spot preemptions in us-west1 between 02:10–03:00 UTC. Several short interactive sessions got killed and some small training shards failed to checkpoint. Logs show a bunch of preemptible term signals from the cloud provider. :frown:
kevin: Ugh. Was it a single instance type getting reclaimed or broad across types?
olivia: I pulled the node event stream — it was concentrated on p4-a100s and nvidia-a10g in the us-west1 zone, but some p3 instances also popped. Looks capacity-constrained (maintenance + marketplace demand).
sre-bot: incident-alert: spot-preemptions-us-west1 detected (count=42 in 50m). Affected clusters: batch-gpu-usw1, dev-notebooks-usw1. Suggested mitigation: drain & cordon, fallback to reserved pool if policy allows.
ben: Thanks for the alert. Two quick asks: (1) can we automatically move interactive sessions to reserved or dedicated when preemptions > X%? (2) For batch, can we requeue to other regions or cheaper CPU-only queue?
maria: Agree. Idea: introduce a "fair-spot" scheduler layer that classifies jobs as interactive vs batch, and enforces: high-priority interactive gets 20% reserved headroom; batch gets preemptible pool only and is backoff-friendly. Also add an off-peak shift policy to expand spot pool at 02:00–06:00 UTC when costs are lowest.
kevin: I sketched a rough k8s Queue CRD config we could start with — simple and enforceable at the gateway:```yamlqueues:
  - name: interactive
    priority: 100
    reserved_headroom_percent: 20
    fallback: dedicated
  - name: batch
    priority: 50
    preemptible_only: true
    max_attempts: 5
    backoff: 15m
  - name: low_cost_shift
    window: "02:00-06:00 UTC"
    scale_spot_pool: +30%```
olivia: Nice. A couple of gotchas: (a) cross-region failover needs image and dataset locality checks, (b) autoscaler must incorporate regional spot price signals to avoid thrashing, (c) telemetry — we need token-level SLA metrics to show impact.
ben: For interruption handling: require app-level checkpointing for batch jobs. For PyTorch training, provide a wrapper that checkpoints to s3 every N steps and exits gracefully on SIGTERM. Add a small library and example in devex.
maria: Agreed. Also propose a soft-throttling middleware: when spot preemptions exceed threshold, throttle new interactive sessions to save headroom for currently active ones (less disruptive UX than killing). Throttle = reduce new session accepts by 30% for 10 min if preemptions > 15% across zone.
kevin: Implementation note: use token-bucket on the session-gateway. We already have rate limiter hooks — add a preemptible-aware limiter. Pseudo:```python
if zone_preempt_pct(zone) > 0.15:
    session_accept_rate *= 0.7
```
maria: Can we also tag batch jobs with "retryable=true" and set QoS class so kube evicting favors batch pods?
olivia: Yes — set pod priorityClass=batch-low, add terminationGracePeriodSeconds and preStop hook to trigger checkpoint. For cross-region fallback, gate by dataset-size < 50GB or use remote dataset mounting.
ben: Cost target reminder: keep average GPU-hour spot utilization > 70% and reduce reserved idle headroom to < 8% for non-critical pools. This fair queue design should help.
kevin: Quick ask to infra infra-ops: can we add a dashboard for "spot pressure" per zone with three metrics: preempt_rate, spare_capacity_percent, job_requeue_rate? If we get those we can tune thresholds instead of guessing.
maria: I'll file the infra ticket and attach suggested metrics + playbook steps. For now, let's enable a canary: implement the queue CRD and limiter on dev cluster in us-west1 for one week, monitor, then roll to prod. @olivia can you own the dev rollout?
olivia: Yep — will schedule the rollout tomorrow 01:00 UTC, will also add test harness for checkpointing.
ben: I'll add the devex wrapper and one training example.
sre-bot: note: runbook updated with 'fair-spot-queue' steps and rollback plan.
maria: Great. Thanks everyone. Will post ticket link and timeline in this thread.
